clue.text: It may be Venetian marble, but that's as far as one can go

definitions.text: that's as far as one can go

parts.note: a Venetian is a kind of window blind with horizontal slats
an alley is a large playing marble

explanation.surface: Someone muses on Venetian marble as the limit of what can be achieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venetian marble' reads as stone from Venice; it splits into a Venetian (a blind) and a marble (an alley).
explanation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac with no way through is where a traveller can go no further, literally or as a hopeless course.

clue.text: Amelia's slip

definitions.meaning: the loose Turkish-style trousers worn under a short skirt took their name from the American reformer Amelia who championed them in the 1850s
a slip is a blunder, an embarrassing mistake

explanation.surface: A woman named Amelia makes an error, or perhaps wears an undergarment.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a garment Amelia Bloomer popularised, and in British slang a gaffe or howler.

clue.text: Create ski specially for winter sports person

indicators.note: specially suggests the letters are arranged in a special new way for the purpose

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to design a custom ski for a winter athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who glides on blades over a frozen rink takes part in a winter sport.

clue.text: Practice progressively unnecessary for strippers

parts.note: a final run-through in full costume, read as something strippers would find ever less needed as the act goes on and clothes come off

explanation.surface: Exotic dancers find rehearsal less and less necessary as their act proceeds.
explanation.definitionFit: The last full rehearsal before a show, in costume, is practice; strippers end up wearing nothing, so the costume matters less and less.

clue.text: As socialist committed, before one's time

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the others in the answer

parts.note: committed in the sense of consigned or entrusted, as when something is left to someone's care
one's read as one is, written I'S

explanation.surface: Someone describes themselves as a dedicated socialist who was ahead of their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'committed' looks like an adjective qualifying socialist, but it gives LEFT (consigned, handed over).
explanation.definitionFit: A person on the political left, such as a socialist, is called a left-winger.

clue.text: Flexible people ultimately remain in charge

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word people

parts.note: to remain is to last or endure

explanation.surface: Adaptable folk end up keeping control.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stretchy that springs back can bend and give, so it is pliable.

clue.text: Little woman in punt with husband

parts.note: to punt is to place a bet, in British betting slang
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogy

explanation.surface: A small woman sits in a flat-bottomed boat alongside her spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests a boat on a river; it means a wager. 'Little woman' points to Alcott's novel Little Women, in which Beth March is one of the four sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beth March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's Little Women.

clue.text: Enthusiastic wave to audience

indicators.note: to an audience means as heard by listeners, so the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: an eagre is a tidal bore, a single large wave surging up a river such as the Severn

explanation.surface: A keen performer waves to the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: An eagre (also spelt eager) is a tidal bore on English rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and impatient to do something is the sense of the adjective.

clue.text: Darby, for example, has to manage thriftily

definitions.meaning: Darby of Darby and Joan, the proverbial devoted elderly married couple, is the archetypal married man
to use resources sparingly and carefully, conserving them for later

explanation.surface: An old man named Darby must learn to budget.
explanation.walkthrough: Darby and Joan are a British byword for a loving elderly married couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Darby is the married man of the pair; as a verb the word means to conserve resources economically.

clue.text: Place that sells juice satisfying Victoria, for one

parts.note: a filling meal is a satisfying one
Victoria is a major London railway station

explanation.surface: A café sells fruit juice that sates a woman named Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'juice' is slang for petrol, not fruit drink; Victoria is a London terminus, not a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is informal for fuel, and a forecourt where drivers buy petrol sells it.

clue.text: Central section of wardrobe seeming heavy

indicators.note: the central section of the words wardrobe seeming contains the answer in an unbroken run

explanation.surface: The middle part of a wardrobe looks weighty.
explanation.definitionFit: Very overweight people are described as heavy.

clue.text: Very hot ordinary seaman in waders

parts.note: flaming means burning, extremely hot
OS is the naval abbreviation for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A sweltering junior sailor stands in rubber fishing boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waders' looks like boots for wading; it means wading birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-legged pink birds that stand in shallow lagoons are wading birds.

clue.text: Improvised fashion garment

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it
a shift is a simple loose dress

explanation.surface: An improvised piece of fashion clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put together temporarily from whatever is to hand is improvised.

clue.text: Sea receding round very immature creature

indicators.note: round means the reversed sea goes around the next piece
receding means moving back, so the sea's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Aral Sea in Central Asia

explanation.surface: The sea retreats around an extremely young animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receding' turns ARAL to LARA; 'round' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub or caterpillar is the young feeding stage of an insect before it matures.

clue.text: Give ground for a sanctuary

definitions.meaning: to give ground is to fall back or withdraw
a sanctuary is a quiet place of refuge

explanation.surface: Surrender land to create a sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means withdraw; as a noun a secluded refuge.

clue.text: Sugary sweetheart embraced by Frank

indicators.note: embraced by means the sweetheart is held inside the frank word

parts.note: frank means candid, honest
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

explanation.surface: A man called Frank hugs his sugary-sweet beloved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but means candid; 'sweetheart' is the heart of sweet, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit preserved in syrup is candied, coated or soaked in sugar.

clue.text: Elected successor of Winston could be merciless

parts.note: a party that is elected is in, in power
Clement Attlee succeeded Winston Churchill as British Prime Minister in 1945

explanation.surface: Churchill's elected successor might prove ruthless.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee followed Winston Churchill as Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh weather is described this way, and the word's older sense is unmerciful, lacking clemency.

clue.text: Flourish from bugler at the front to give encouragement

indicators.note: at the front points to the first letter of the word bugler

parts.note: to urge on is to encourage

explanation.surface: A bugler at the head of the troops plays a fanfare to cheer them on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flourish' suggests a bugle fanfare; it is the verb meaning thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow vigorously and thrive is to flourish.

clue.text: One of Peel's hounds involved in perilous hunt

definitions.meaning: in the song D'ye ken John Peel, about a Cumbrian huntsman, the hounds include Ranter
in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark

explanation.surface: A hound from a famous pack joins a dangerous chase.
explanation.walkthrough: John Peel was a Cumbrian huntsman celebrated in an English folk song naming his hounds; the perilous hunt is Carroll's Snark hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellman is named among Peel's hounds in the song, and the Bellman leads Carroll's Snark hunters.

clue.text: New university getting free kind of energy

parts.note: clear means free of obstruction or charges

explanation.surface: A new university gets free power.
explanation.definitionFit: Power produced by splitting atoms is atomic energy.

clue.text: Contemptible people belonging to separate schools

parts.note: belonging to a group is being in it
sects are separate schools of thought, breakaway factions

explanation.surface: Despised folk who attend different schools.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects is a figurative insult for lowly, contemptible persons.

clue.text: Cold-blooded type with hidden depths

parts.note: reads as a cold, unfeeling person with a secret inner life, but describes a floating mass of frozen water mostly below the surface

explanation.surface: A heartless person who turns out to have unexpected depths.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, aloof person is called this, and most of a floating mass of ice lies unseen below water.

clue.text: Legislator involved in treason

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lawmaker implicated in treachery.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a senate, such as in the US Congress, makes laws.

clue.text: Turn to celebrate prize in America

indicators.note: turn means the word for celebrate is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: to revel is to celebrate noisily

explanation.surface: An American party marking an award.
explanation.walkthrough: In America 'prize' is a spelling of prise, to force open with leverage.
explanation.definitionFit: To prise something open is to apply a bar for leverage, and American spelling writes prise as prize.

clue.text: Rendezvous with beautiful woman finally changed

indicators.note: finally changed means the last letter of the woman's name is swapped for another

parts.note: Venus, the goddess of love, stands for a beautiful woman

explanation.surface: A date with a beautiful woman ends differently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally changed' swaps the last letter of VENUS, S, for E.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting place for an event is the place of rendezvous.

clue.text: Thanks to this section, the Emperor came to life

definitions.text: Thanks to this section, the Emperor came to life

parts.words: Thanks to this section, the Emperor came to life
parts.note: the legend that Julius Caesar was delivered surgically through his mother's abdomen gives the name of the operation

explanation.surface: Thanks to this passage of a text, the Emperor became a living character.
explanation.definitionFit: The surgical delivery of a baby through the abdomen is traditionally said to be named after Julius Caesar's birth.

clue.text: Metal bat Australian opener's seen breaking

annotationWithheld.why: Metal bat Australian opener's seen breaking (9): A (Australian opener) and SEEN account for five letters of MANGANESE, but no sense of 'bat' gives the remaining M, N, G, A; the clue's mechanism could not be confirmed
annotationWithheld.clue: Metal bat Australian opener's seen breaking

clue.text: Defective retina almost unresponsive

indicators.note: defective means faulty, so the letters are rearranged
almost means the word retina is taken without its final letter

explanation.surface: A faulty retina barely reacts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RETINA to RETIN; 'Defective' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inert is inactive, showing no reaction.

clue.text: Teller's ability to detect those voting against

indicators.note: a teller is one who tells or speaks, so the word is as spoken

parts.note: a nose for something is a knack for detecting it

explanation.surface: A parliamentary vote-counter can sniff out the dissenters.
explanation.walkthrough: In Parliament tellers count the votes, which makes 'Teller's' look like part of the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: In a parliamentary division the votes against are recorded as the noes.

clue.text: Forebear reporting outrageously about love

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
outrageously suggests wild disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: An ancestor reports scandalously on romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor from whom a family descends is a forebear.
